rule.description: god-class: a module-level class that owns at least 25 non-dunder methods or at least 400 owned statements concentrates distinct responsibilities that belong in separate, cohesive classes. Every matched god class also lists the same-package classes it imports that still stash constructor state but define no behavior (the drained owners of the absorbed responsibilities).

checks.description: One facade class owns proxy discovery coordination together with judge provisioning/verification and the full per-proxy validation pipeline.
checks.detected_relation: oversized class -> responsibilities absorbed from its collaborators
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: A single class body defines far too much distinct behavior for one ownership unit: the coordinator's methods now inline judge handling and proxy validation that used to live in the collaborator classes of the same package.

matches.evidence: Broker (class body starting at line 46) defines 29 non-dunder methods and owns 580 statements, exceeding both threshold dimensions (25 methods, 400 statements). Its body implements judge defaulting and building, judge DNS resolution and HTTP verification, shared judge availability and per-scheme event gating, random judge selection, checking-plan setup, DNSBL screening, retrying connect/negotiate checks, raw test-request crafting, response decompression, response validation, anonymity-level grading, and strict type filtering, in addition to the original gathering, queueing, serving, limit, and stats orchestration.

checks.description: Same-package classes imported by the oversized owner keep only constructor state and define no behavior of their own anymore.
checks.detected_relation: god-class module -> imported collaborator class with zero owned non-dunder methods
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The responsibilities inlined in the god class were taken from these imported collaborators; their names and constructors still promise those roles, but the classes no longer own any of the behavior, so distinct roles no longer have distinct owners.

matches.evidence: Checker is imported and instantiated by the Broker module yet defines 0 non-dunder methods; the 24 owned statements that remain are exclusively its constructor's state setup, so none of the proxy-validation work the class is named for lives in it.

Judge is imported by the Broker module yet defines 0 non-dunder methods; the 22 owned statements that remain are exclusively its constructor's state setup, while judge discovery, verification, availability bookkeeping, and selection are defined in the Broker body.

excluded: proxybroker/proxy.py::Proxy (22 methods, 237 statements) stays below both threshold dimensions; it is one cohesive per-proxy descriptor and does not participate in the absorbed responsibilities.
proxybroker/server.py::Server (9 methods) and ProxyPool (3 methods) own the local serving pool; they are command consumers of the facade, not absorbed owners.
proxybroker/providers.py::Provider (10 methods) and the per-site provider subclasses keep their scraping behavior and are not imported as drained collaborators.
proxybroker/resolver.py::Resolver and proxybroker/negotiators.py protocol classes retain their methods; they are shared infrastructure, outside the absorbed responsibility set.
Exception classes in proxybroker/errors.py declare no behavior by design (no constructor state); they are data-only declarations, not drained owners.
proxybroker/checker.py::ProxyChecker is a deprecation shim that is not imported by the god-class module and keeps its deprecation-warning constructor.
